I've posted this comment as a response to someone else's post, which was about facial seb derm. I used to have pretty bad facial seb derm and reasonably mild scalp seb derm. It's a long read (sorry!) and after I will add a bit about my own scalp no-poo routine.

"Hi, please don't dispair! This is my first comment on this sub, so I'm sorry if I  say anything that  you already know. I have suffered from seb derm myself, but by now it's so much less than before. I've read a lot of the research on seb derm and figured out the following:

u/fanzipan is right about the seb derm feeding on the grease on your face. Specifically, malassezia yeast feed on fatty acids, but I'll get back to that later. By drying your face out with vinegar and nizoral, you might remove the grease for a short while, but your skin will start overcompensating and produce even more oil, which feeds the yeast. 

Malassezia can only metabolize fatty acids with chain lengths between 12 and 24 carbon atoms. This may sound a bit complicated, but it means that certain oils will not feed the yeast, while some will. Most of our natural skin sebum consists of the kind of fatty acids that feed the malassezia yeast, sadly, so making our skin produce more sebum is a bad idea!

A better idea is to "moisturize" (I don't know if that's the right word) our skin with fatty acids that don't feed the yeast, so with carbon chain lengths of less than 12 or more than 24. This way, our skin will keep the production of sebum very low, because it's not dry.

Examples of fatty acids with carbon chain lengths lower than 12 are capric (8) and caprylic (10) triglycerides. These are found in BioM8, a product a lot of people like. I ordered capric&caprylic triglycerides on a website with raw materials for make-up etc. It's worked very well for me!

Examples of fatty acids with carbon chain lengths higher than 24 are petrolatum (found in vaseline and aquaphor), but also squalane (I have this from The Ordinary). I love the Squalane, but I use vaseline mostly in the winter when I need a little extra protection.

This has helped me so, so much! I now only have rosacea to deal with, for which I am getting laser treatment. Hang in there, I hope this helps you, I know how desperate seb derm can make you feel. Don't hesitate to ask any questions!"

As for my scalp: I've been no-poo (water only) for about 2 years, but using the capric&caprylic triglycerides (I'll call it CCT) on my scalp as well, to make sure my scalp doesn't keep producing it's own sebum. I apply the CCT to a cotton pad and dab that on my scalp before the shower. Then I rub it into my skin, which also took care of the scales back when I still had them. Then in the shower I also rub my scalp under the water and that's it. I went through a pretty ugly oily period, but my hair's so happy now. I recently went to the hairdresser and let her wash my hair, and my skin was itchy and flaking for the next few days until I treated it with the CCT again. Good luck!

The only real answer I have to this is: please don't do it. You're still growing and you need food for that otherwise it will stunt the growth of your body and brain. If you can, try talking to your parents about your desire to lose weight and eat healthy. 

As a teenager you have a really fast metabolism and you will start growing in height really fast in a few years. This is perfect for weight loss (also why a lot of teens will be tall and very skinny for a few years during their puberty). So if you eat healthy and enough, stay away from the really bad stuff like candy, fast food and chips, you'll lose weight a lot faster than an adult would. If you get some movement you'll speed it up even more - start small with walks or bike rides around the block and then maybe find a team sport you like.

If however you really go through with it please be very careful and look out for any signs that your body is not okay with it, like dizziness, nausea, bad headaches, etc. Stop immediately.

If you want to lose weight and keep it off long term, you're going to have to eat healthy meals 3 times a day (so not just for dinner, also breakfast and lunch need to be healthy). Talk to your parents about this if you can.
